method.value: Gaussian plus polynomial fits of line centres at each beam position; Monte-Carlo errors

evidence.quote: we performed Gaussian fits (the sum of a Gaussian and a 1 [st] or 2 [nd] degree polynomial) of the line profiles in their central parts
Repeating this procedure 300 times, the dispersion in the fitted positions provided an estimate of the error bars

results_numeric.quantity: HNC equatorial jet max speed at ~1000 km

evidence.quote: equatorial jet with ~350 m/s maximum speed
the bulk of HNC is located above 870±40 km altitude
best fit cutoff altitude of 630±30 km
a ~140 K mesopause, located at 800±50 km altitude

findings_qualitative.value: Strong prograde winds extend into the thermosphere, becoming an equatorial jet with altitude.

evidence.quote: strong prograde winds extend up to the thermosphere, with the circulation progressively turning into an equatorial jet regime as altitude increases

claims.hypothesis: Do strong prograde winds extend to Titan's thermosphere?

evidence.quote: reaching ~340 m/s at 1000 km

claims.finding: HNC is thermospheric, GCR plays minor role

evidence.quote: the HNC distribution is restricted to Titan’s thermosphere above ~870 km altitude

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gravitational tides rejected as source of strong winds

evidence.quote: Gravitational tides [28] are not promising for explaining the strong wind speeds we measure

limitations_admitted.value: Wind modelling ignores altitude-dependent Doppler shifts in 2D; approximate.

evidence.quote: this is still an approximate way of modelling the data
